english.title: Sponsor fail to report on the safety of the participants of clinical trials of investigational medicinal products

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Medicines for Human Use Clinical trials Regulations 2004

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the sponsor of a clinical trial referred to in regulation A32(1) of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004, failed to provide the licensing authority with a report on the safety of the participants of each investigational medicinal product tested, within the period of 60 days, beginning with the day after the day on which the reporting year ended namely, **(..SPECIFY DATE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 35(1), 49(1)(j) and 52 of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
within the period of 60 days beginning with the day after the day on which the reporting year ended
sponsor failed to report
on the safety of participants in clinical trials testing investigational medicinal products
to the licensing authority

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Regulation 51 of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 provides a defence of due diligence.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 3 months imprisonment and / or a fine
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
